comparisons.evidence:
A bar (MCC 5813) serves alcohol on the premises, so ALC-01 and
ALC-02 apply to it exactly as they do to a restaurant, and it is never treated as retail under
ALC-03.

Alcohol is **never** reimbursable for APAC-entity employees, including
within client entertainment. This overrides ALC-01 and ALC-02: where those rules would have
permitted alcohol with an attendee count, REG-01 still makes it a **high** exception. For APAC employees REG-01 replaces ALC-01, ALC-02 and
ALC-03: report REG-01 instead of those three. Rules about the merchant, such as MCC-01, still apply.

location.section: APAC entity — employees in IN, JP, SG

comparisons.evidence:
This includes, and is not limited to:
headphones and earbuds, smart watches and fitness trackers, tablets and e-readers, games
consoles, cameras and drones, televisions, portable speakers, and item trackers. Accessories made
for such a device — cases, chargers, screen protectors — count as personal electronics too.
Purchase of any of these on an expense report is a **high** exception, regardless of stated
business purpose.

Two or more receipts by the same employee, at the same merchant
(by merchant name), on the same calendar date, are treated as a deliberate split when each one is
at or below one of these thresholds but together they are above it: the $75 itemization threshold,
when every receipt in the group is non-itemized (DOC-01); the employee's meal cap, compared per person (MEAL-01, REG-02, REG-03); or the $50 gift cap for
one recipient (GIFT-01). This **is** an exception, at **high** severity,
and applies to every receipt in the group. It replaces the threshold rule being split around: report
the split, not a separate breach of that threshold.
